title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatic 'Analysis situs', an attempt at a combinatorial or axiomatic tame topology.
- There is a set M of strata.
- 'Figures' are (roughly) finite unions of strata, ordered by ≤ (sub-figure). Sup and Inf are taken stratum-wise: H = sup of the strata X ≤ H.
- There is a second relation ≼ (a closedness or neighbourhood-type relation governed by axiom C6).
- There is a derived relation ≪, read as 'G is a closed sub-figure of F'. By the next page's definition, G ≪ F means there is a sub-figure F̄ with G ≤ F̄ ≼ F.
- On page 75 he decided he must 'develop the notion of induced neighbourhoods' (voisinages induits). This page states the key proposition for that.

Proposition (p.76). Let G ≪ F and let F' ≤ F be a sub-figure. Then:
- There exists a largest sub-figure G' of G that is ≪ F' (my reading of the word after 'qui').
- G' is the figure induced on F' by G; equivalently, the sub-figure of G induced by the sub-figure F' of F. Its strata are exactly the strata of G that 'satisfy' F'.
- This gives a commutative square: G ≪ F on top, G' ≪ F' below, with G' ≤ G and F' ≤ F.
- G' is an infimum of G and F' for the relation ≪: if K ≪ G and K ≪ F', then K ≪ G'.

Marginal remark. One should say in passing that G' = ∅ ⇔ G is disjoint from F', which he flags as 'non évident'.

Crossed-out proof attempt. Let H ≪ F'. Then every stratum X ≤ H satisfies X ≪ F'. Let G' be the sub-figure generated by the strata Y ∈ G satisfying the condition. Then H ≤ G', because H = sup_{X ≤ H} X ≤ sup_{X ∈ G'} X = G'. He abandons this and restarts on p.77. There G' is identified with G ∩ F̄', and the inf property is reduced via Lemma 1 to axiom C6(b), applied to the square formed by Ḡ ≼ F and Ḡ' ≼ F'.

Topological meaning. If figures are locally closed unions of strata in a stratified space and ≪ is 'closed in', the statement is elementary: G' = G ∩ F' is closed in F', is the largest such piece, and K closed in both G and F' implies K closed in G ∩ F'. The content of the page is that these 'restriction of closed pieces' and 'meet' properties are derivable purely from his axioms C1–C7. That makes the induced-figure (base-change or restriction) operation available in the axiomatic theory. This mirrors restricting a closed subset along a locally closed inclusion, i.e. the poset-level shadow of pulling back closed immersions.
errors: No mathematical error in the stated proposition; in the topological model it is correct. The proof on this page is crossed out and incomplete: it ends at 'D'autre part, G' ≪' and confuses roles (it starts 'Soit H une sous-figure de H', and uses 'Y ≪ H' where 'Y ≪ F'' seems intended). The actual proof is redone on p.77 via C6.
The claim G' = ∅ ⇔ G ∩ F' = ∅ is asserted but left unproved ('non évident'); it is not established on this page.

ideas.what: Axiomatic theory of 'figures' (finite unions of strata) with relations ≤, ≼, ≪, as a foundation for tame topology
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic tame topology / o-minimal-style stratified structures; poset-theoretic frameworks for stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries (o-minimal structures, 1980s–1998), Shiota, Pillay–Steinhorn–Knight; Grothendieck's call for 'topologie modérée' in Esquisse
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6, programme only; axioms not published

ideas.what: Induced sub-figure: for G ≪ F and F' ≤ F, the largest sub-figure G' of G with G' ≪ F', namely G ∩ F̄'
ideas.modern_name: Restriction of a closed subset to a locally closed subspace (base change of a closed immersion), at the level of a poset of constructible pieces

ideas.what: G' is the infimum of G and F' for the relation ≪
ideas.modern_name: Meet / pullback property of closed embeddings in a lattice of constructible sets

ideas.what: G' = ∅ iff G is disjoint from F', flagged as non-obvious from the axioms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney / Thom–Mather frontier condition (in geometric settings)

missed.claim: Grothendieck flags as a needed but 'non-obvious' consequence of his axioms that the induced figure G' vanishes exactly when G is disjoint from F'. This is part of an unfinished axiomatic tame-topology programme whose axiom system (C1–C7) was never published.
missed.quote: Dire (en passant) que G' = ∅ ⇔ G disjoint de F' (non évident....)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historical interest. It documents how far the axiomatic 'analysis situs' was carried and which properties he found hard to derive. Mathematically it is elementary in all standard models (o-minimal, semialgebraic, subanalytic).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine lattice-theoretic lemma (restriction of closed pieces and existence of meets for ≪) inside Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic tame topology. The programme itself is of historical interest, but this page contains no result unknown to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Line 5–6: 'une plus grande sous-figure F'[?] de G' should almost certainly read 'sous-figure G' de G'; the object constructed is G'.
'qui vérifie F'' is uncertain; context suggests 'qui ≪ F'' (or a word meaning 'is closed in F'').
'induite sur G des figures F' qui vérifient G et F' is an unreliable reading. The sense is 'la sous-figure de G induite par la sous-figure F' de F'.
The diagram at top is G ≪ F over G' and F', with ∨| (≥) arrows; the crossed-out first G is replaced by G'.
The crossed-out 'Dém.' paragraph starts 'Soit H une sous-figure de ...' (probably of G) 'telle que H ≪ F''. The strata condition reads 'Y ∈ G telles que Y ≪ H', likely a slip for F'.
